extract.title: ADR-001: Application architecture for the licensing portal
decisions: Modular monolith: one deployable web application with internal modules (applications, documents, workflow, payments)
Managed relational database for application data
Object storage for uploaded and migrated documents
Scheduled jobs for the nightly finance and student data integrations
Small adapter for the real-time payment provider
Candidate platforms: Azure (App Service, Azure SQL, Blob Storage) or AWS (ECS Fargate, RDS, S3), to be validated
rejected_alternatives: Event-driven microservices (higher cost, complexity and delivery time than the scale requires)
constraints: Must use the existing identity provider
deployment_targets: Azure (selected for this pack, to validate)
conflicts: The ADR status is still Proposed; generate drafts only and get the ADR approved before handing off

assumptions: Migration plan kept as a separate workstream
scaffold.review_notes: Confirm the module list and stack with the delivery team.

assumptions: One API surface served by the web app
Payment uses the provider's redirect flow
api.review_notes: Document size limits and correspondence endpoints are not yet defined.

assumptions: P1v3 plan and S2 database sized for under 500 concurrent users
ZRS storage until RTO/RPO are known
iac.review_notes: Nightly job Functions and payment egress rules are not included yet.

assumptions: Nightly jobs run on Azure Functions
diagram.review_notes: Matches the IaC except Functions, which are still a TODO in the Terraform.

assumptions: Sandbox subscription available for plan runs
readme.review_notes: Update local setup once the stack is confirmed.

checklist.review_notes: Every item traces to ADR-001 or a guardrail.

scaffold.finding: Modules match the ADR decision and stay in one deployable app.
Secrets referenced by name only; .env.example has no values.
Stack choice (Python) is an assumption, not an ADR decision.
scaffold.fix: Confirm the approved stack before creating repositories.

api.finding: Single API surface for the modular monolith; covers applications, documents, workflow and payments.
OIDC security scheme; reviewer endpoints need the reviewer scope; no card data in the contract.
Upload size limit and correspondence templates are not specified.
api.fix: Agree limits and add the correspondence endpoints.

api.finding: Server and issuer URLs are placeholders.

iac.finding: App Service, Azure SQL and Blob Storage match the ADR's Azure candidates.
Location variable is validated to US regions.
The SQL administrator password is hardcoded and there is no Key Vault, which breaks the 'no secrets in code' guardrail.
iac.fix: Generate the password, store it in Key Vault and give the web app a managed identity with a Key Vault reference.

iac.finding: Application Insights backed by Log Analytics is wired into the web app.
SKUs are assumptions and Functions for nightly jobs are missing.
iac.fix: Validate SKUs after a peak-window load test and add the Functions.

diagram.finding: Shows one web app, database, storage, jobs and payment adapter as decided.
Secrets flow from Key Vault through managed identity.
Diagram shows Key Vault and Functions, which the first IaC draft does not create.
diagram.fix: Keep the diagram and IaC consistent after refinement.

readme.finding: States the ADR it implements and that the platform choice is a candidate.
Tells developers never to commit .env and to use sandbox subscriptions only.
Marks all files as drafts and lists open questions.

checklist.finding: Items trace to ADR decisions and consequences.
Covers residency, peak load, accessibility and open availability targets.
Includes telemetry, audit and alerting items.
Requires draft labels, validation of service names and sandbox validation.

refine.instruction: Remove the hardcoded SQL password: generate it, store it in Key Vault and let the web app read it through a managed identity.

assumptions: P1v3 plan and S2 database sized for under 500 concurrent users
ZRS storage until RTO/RPO are known
result.review_notes: Added Key Vault, a generated SQL admin password stored as a secret, a system-assigned identity for the web app with the Key Vault Secrets User role, and a Key Vault reference app setting. Admin login is now a variable.

review.finding: Still App Service, Azure SQL and Blob Storage as decided.
Location variable is validated to US regions.
No secret literals; password generated and held in Key Vault; app uses managed identity.
Application Insights wired into the web app.
SKUs are assumptions and Functions for nightly jobs are still missing.
review.fix: Validate SKUs after a peak-window load test and add the Functions.
